speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Transport how will the Ministry fix the problem-prone Bukit Panjang LRT system and whether there are plans to overhaul the entire system or to replace it with a more reliable transport mode to better serve the residents living there.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Typical examples include the Sentosa Express and skytrains in airports to connect terminal buildings.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The decision to implement the Bukit Panjang LRT (BPLRT), required shoe-horning an LRT system into a built-up town.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This has posed significant engineering challenges, requiring the LRT to make sharp bends and over undulating terrain.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The BPLRT's reliability has therefore been unsatisfactory, despite significant efforts by the Land Transport Authority (LTA), Singapore Mass Rapid Transit (SMRT) and the train manufacturer, Bombardier over many years.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: There are two main technical challenges for BPLRT.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: First, the current design of the power rail.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It requires three points of contact simultaneously with the trains' collector shoes.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Any misalignment could trigger a power trip or even dislodge the collector shoes, causing a disruption.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The sharp bends and undulating terrain further contribute to this problem.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Second, the current track layout in the vicinity of Bukit Panjang station and the LRT service routing require trains leaving the Bukit Panjang station to constantly switch tracks.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This has made the switch point a critical vulnerability.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Fortunately, there are now better technology and designs available, compared to 17 years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: First, we are studying a redesign of Bukit Panjang station, its track layout and the BPLRT routing to remove the need to constantly switch tracks and to smoothen some parts of the alignment.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The road network in Bukit Panjang will not be able to cope.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The news headline of that possibility has caused great anxiety and concerns to our residents.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But notwithstanding the service breakdowns that they had experienced, I think they still want the LRT system because replacing it with a bus system is just not practical.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister, whilst we are looking into how we can significantly upgrade the system to enhance the reliability, in the interim, can LTA improve on the response to breakdowns because there could still be some more breakdowns as we discover new things, whether we can have provision of more buses within the town, feeder service so that in the event there is a disruption or breakdown, the buses can be re-deployed to respond to breakdowns and to minimise inconvenience to our residents?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The short answer is yes and we do.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And I think the Member would know that if you look at recent incidents of handling, things have improved.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But for BPLRT, in particular, a lot of energy is right now also spent on sorting out the medium-term solutions which we need to clean up within the next four or five years.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I am reasonably confident that we can tackle this problem.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I am more confident about this than my bet on who is the next American President.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Yes, we are equally concerned over the next President as well.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I just want to also ask the Minister, from my interactions with the SMRT staff and engineers looking after the BPLRT system, I get the sense they are not placing enough priority, or maybe they are not resourced enough to deal with some of these operational problems that they have.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: And maybe, indeed, they were also thinking and hoping that the system will be scrapped.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister, as we look at this whole change to enhance the system, whether it makes sense to have this system run by a separate entity on a not-for-profit basis so that we get the system stabilised first before we look at how we can worry about other commercial considerations.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I have worked with them for one year now.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I have been in the Ministry for one year.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I spend a lot of time on the ground talking to the people from top, senior level to the junior level, including many of the engineers, assistant engineers and technicians working their guts out in the trenches.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I cannot speak for the previous leadership of SMRT but, for the current team, they are taking this very seriously, not just BPLRT but the entire MRT network, because they know that whatever they do or fail to do have major impact.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As I said a couple of days ago, more than two million commuters use our service every day and we can make a difference to their lives.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is a very important function that we play.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, I am less interested in the past but on the way forward.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In fact, in the past few months, I believe that things are improving.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I take trains, and many commuters come forward to express their direct experience because they are daily users of the service.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Just last week, on a train, one secondary school student came to me.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: He recognised me and he came for a chat.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, I asked, "Do you use the train service every day?" He said, "Yes, every day.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: How else can I move around?" I asked, "Have you personally experienced disruptions?" He said, "Many." I was very sad to hear that.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, I asked, "When was your last disruption experience?" He said, "December last year." I said, "That means this year, things have improved?" He said, "Oh yes."

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: For the Minister of Transport, I have one question.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, as a company, they look at it from a total portfolio point of view.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As I said earlier, the current team does not look at it from a pure bottom-line angle, rather that they are a public service provider, they have a duty to perform, and their job is to deliver it to the best of their ability.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why we have an independent Public Transport Council (PTC) to ensure the long-term viability of all the train services.
